What Needs You
Show Everything

What Needs You is where the world tells you things and asks you things. A notice says what happened: groceries you couldn’t pay for, a commitment you slept through, a welcome to the school. A question carries its answers as buttons, such as File It or Keep The Account, and Dismiss. The number beside Home on the menu is how many of both are waiting.

Where To Find It
Home, The What Needs You Panel.
When You Can Use It
From “What Needs You”.
Show Me Where
What To Press
Open Home and read What Needs You: questions first, then notices.
Press one of a question’s answers to act on it there. It does what the same button on its own screen does.
Press Go There to open the screen a question or a notice is about.
Press Dismiss to take a question off the list without answering it.
Press Mark N Read, at the top of the panel, to mark every unread notice read at once.
Press Show All N, under the notices, to see every unread one before you do: the panel draws the six most important first, and Show The Six Most Important goes back to them.
Press a question’s or a notice’s title to open it: how urgent or important it is, when it closes, and where it sits in the list.

How This Works

Yale Health covers you while you’re at the School. Public cover depends on your income in a month. Medicaid (Medi-Cal in California, HUSKY D in Connecticut) covers you up to 138% of the poverty line. In New York the Essential Plan covers you up to 200%, and in Connecticut Covered Connecticut covers you up to 175% of the previous year’s line. Each is open at any time, with no premium. Covered Connecticut is for an income over HUSKY D’s line, whatever your immigration status, and comes with the premium tax credit from 100% of the poverty line. From 2027 a student in F-1 status or a graduate on OPT gets no premium tax credit. From 2027 Medicaid also has work rules. You meet them in any month you spend some of at the School, or in a month with $580.00 of income (pay, interest, a benefit or a pension). In Connecticut that’s the month before you apply, or any one of the 6 months before a renewal. You also meet them if you’re 65 or over, if you get SNAP under its own work rules, or if you ask for a hospital stay to count. If you don’t meet them, a notice gives you 30 days from when you receive it to answer before an application is denied or cover ends. An ending is announced at least 10 days ahead, at the end of a month. On a marketplace plan you pay the whole premium each month, and your tax return gives back what’s over your share of income, a nonresident’s 1040-NR too.
